title: Filtered projective middle module and component maps before taking kernels
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $M\in\mathrm{ModuleCat}^{v}(R)$, and $E$ a linearly ordered type with well-founded strict order, with arbitrary universe. Let $F:E\to\mathrm{Submodule}_R(M)$ be monotone and exhaustive. For each $e$ let $P(e)$ be a supplied projective resolution [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension] of $Q_e=F_e/((\sup_{i<e}F_i)\cap F_e)$ [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. There exist a categorically projective $B\in\mathrm{ModuleCat}^{v}(R)$, an $R$-linear map $b:B\to M$, and monotone exhaustive submodules $H_e\subseteq B$ such that $b(H_e)=F_e$. For every $e$, either $H_e=\sup_{i<e}H_i$, or there are a surjective linear map $p_e:H_e\to P(e)_0$ with kernel $(\sup_{i<e}H_i)\cap H_e$ and a linear map $a_e:H_e\to F_e$ such that $F_e\hookrightarrow M$ composed with $a_e$ equals $b|_{H_e}$, and the augmentation composed with $p_e$ equals the quotient map composed with $a_e$. The construction uses the direct sum [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules] over active indices. No assertion about the kernel of $b$ is made.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0D1U (lemma-colimit-projective-dimension), direct-sum presentation construction; adaptation to supplied degree-zero projectives and active-index universe reduction from the parent node. Source also read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D1U.

proof.text: Set V_e to the predecessor supremum. Call e active when F_e differs from V_e (equivalently the successive quotient is nonzero). Choose a witness in F_e outside V_e; monotonicity gives an injection of active stages into M. Use small_of_injective and equivShrink to index the construction in universe v. For each shrunk active index lift the supplied augmentation through the quotient epimorphism with Projective.factorThru; its commuting identity follows from factorThru_comp.

Construct B as the dependent finitely supported functions on the shrunk active indices, with values the supplied projective degree-zero objects. Define b using DFinsupp.lsum of the lifts followed by inclusions. Prove categorical projectivity by factorThru on each summand and lhom_ext. Define H_e by vanishing of coordinates at indices greater than e. Prove monotonicity pointwise and exhaustion by DFinsupp.induction, taking the maximum of the bound for the old support and the new index; hcover at zero supplies an index for the zero vector.

Prove the forward image inclusion by expressing a vector as the finite sum of its single-coordinate vectors and using monotonicity. For the reverse inclusion use well-founded induction. At an active stage surjectivity of the augmentation gives a single-coordinate lift of the quotient class; mk_eq_zero shows that the remainder lies in V_e. At an inactive stage take the single-coordinate contribution to be zero. The supremum of earlier F_i lies in b(H_e), because induction lifts each earlier F_i and monotonicity includes the earlier H_i in H_e. Add the lifted remainder and the current contribution. This uses lattice map monotonicity rather than identifying a chain supremum with its union, and covers the empty predecessor set.

Express any vector whose support is strictly before e as a finite sum of single-coordinate vectors in earlier H_i. At an inactive stage all coordinates allowed in H_e lie strictly before e, giving H_e equal to its predecessor supremum. At an active stage use lapply restricted to H_e. The single-coordinate inclusion proves surjectivity; injectivity of the index map and the support condition identify its kernel with the predecessor supremum pulled back to H_e. Codomain-restrict b to obtain a_e. Subtract the e-coordinate from a vector in H_e; the difference lies in the projection kernel and hence in the predecessor supremum. Its b-image lies in V_e, so the quotient equality follows from Quotient.eq and the commuting identity for the supplied lift.

mathlib_searches.query: A filtered projective module mapping onto a well ordered union of submodules with component projections onto projective presentations of the successive quotients
projective presentation of a module with well ordered filtration and projective resolutions of successive quotients
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits, including ModuleCat.projectiveResolution and CategoryTheory.ProjectiveResolution.of, ofComplex, instProjectiveXNatOfComplex, instHasProjectiveResolutions. These supply resolution infrastructure, not the filtered direct-sum construction.
Six hits concerning map/comap lattice identities, including Submodule.comap_iSup_map_of_injective and Submodule.biSup_comap_subtype_eq_top. None constructs the filtered presentation.

Mathlib hits for partialSum are unrelated. Local rg on lean/Sheaf/RingTheory and lean/WeilConjectures finds only the parent projection theorem and its consumers; the consumers depend on the parent and cannot be used.

theorem exists_projective_presentation_component_data
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (M : ModuleCat.{v} R)
    {E : Type w} [LinearOrder E] [IsWellOrder E (· < ·)]
    (F : E → Submodule R M) (hF : Monotone F)
    (hcover : ∀ x : M, ∃ e : E, x ∈ F e)
    (P : ∀ e : E, ProjectiveResolution
      (ModuleCat.of R ((F e) ⧸
        ((⨆ i : {j : E // j < e}, F i.val).comap (F e).subtype)))) :
    ∃ (B : ModuleCat.{v} R) (_ : Projective B) (b : B →ₗ[R] M)
      (H : E → Submodule R B),
      Monotone H ∧ (∀ x : B, ∃ e : E, x ∈ H e) ∧
      (∀ e : E, (H e).map b = F e) ∧
      ∀ e : E,
        H e = ⨆ i : {j : E // j < e}, H i.val ∨
        ∃ p : H e →ₗ[R] (P e).complex.X 0,
          Function.Surjective p ∧
          p.ker = (⨆ i : {j : E // j < e}, H i.val).comap (H e).subtype ∧
          ∃ a : H e →ₗ[R] F e,
            (F e).subtype.comp a = b.comp (H e).subtype ∧
            ((P e).π.f 0).hom.comp p =
              ((⨆ i : {j : E // j < e}, F i.val).comap (F e).subtype).mkQ.comp a
